title: Crosswalk Benchmark: New York RAISE Act vs California SB-53 Frontier Requirements

original_idea.body:
# Crosswalk Benchmark: New York RAISE Act vs California SB-53 Frontier Requirements

**Problem:** US states are passing frontier AI laws (California's frontier law, New York's analogue) with overlapping-but-divergent requirements. There is no public, clause-level crosswalk measuring where the obligations align, diverge, or leave gaps.

**Direction:** Build a structured crosswalk of the two laws' frontier-developer obligations (transparency, safety plans, incident reporting, thresholds), coding each requirement as same/stricter/looser/absent across the two. Produce a comparison matrix and quantify the harmonization gap, flagging requirements that could create compliance arbitrage.

**Why it matters:** Sub-national fragmentation is a live governance problem; a reproducible legal crosswalk supports harmonization efforts and needs only public statutory text, well within a beginner's reach.

**Relevant context:** Cooley analysis 'New York's Frontier AI Law Gets a California Makeover' (2026); California frontier AI transparency law; EU AI Act as a comparison anchor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Legal harmonization crosswalk has a vague, indirect link to catastrophic-risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Clause-level coding of two public statutes; beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two laws, defined obligations, comparison matrix.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public statutory text; independent crosswalk (law firms also do this).

novelty.reasoning: Informal legal comparisons exist; a structured crosswalk may be open.
